title: The token screen in a clinic waiting room
summary: Show patients an honest wait time on a wall screen and on their own phones.
context: Sampige Clinics has 60 outpatient centres. Patients take a token, then watch a screen on the wall or a page on their phone. Doctors see people at uneven speeds, some leave for tests and come back, and emergencies jump the queue.
A receptionist updates the queue from a browser. When the wall screen falls behind, patients crowd the desk to ask, which slows everything further.
must_handle: The wall screen runs for weeks unattended and recovers by itself after a network drop.
A patient's page keeps working on a slow phone and uses little data.
A wait estimate is a range, and it must not jump around every few seconds.
A screen in a public room must never show a patient's name in full.
A page out of date for more than a minute says so.
show_in_answer: The parts of the page and where each one's data comes from.
How updates reach the browser, and how it recovers after a gap.
How the wait range is worked out and smoothed.
What the screen shows when it has lost contact.
